Subject: Question: Invoice retention when user requests data erasure

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question from our compliance team: when an end user submits a data deletion request, what parts of our billing/usage records does Redwood preserve for accounting and audit purposes? Specifically:

- Do you keep invoice records (invoice number, amount, billing period) even if the user’s account data is erased?
- How long are detailed usage events retained vs. the invoice/ledger?
- Can you provide a redacted invoice export (no PII) that would satisfy our auditors?

We have a couple of auditors asking for a written statement so we can map to our financial records. Happy to hop on a quick call if that’s easier.

Hi Sophie — thanks for raising this. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps.

1) Invoice records: preserved. We retain invoice artifacts (invoice number, invoice PDF, billed amount, billing period, tax and payment status) to satisfy accounting and regulatory obligations. Those are preserved separately from user-generated content.

2) Usage events: detailed event-level logs (full request payloads, prompts) are retained for a shorter operational window (default 90 days) unless otherwise configured on a Dedicated/Private deployment.

3) Redacted exports: yes — we can provide a compliance-friendly export that includes invoice headers, line item totals, timestamps, and hashed user identifiers (one-way salted hash) instead of raw PII.

I’ve attached a short doc summarizing the current retention windows and our suggested evidence bundle for auditors (billing-retention-summary.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
- Neha: can you confirm the finance/GAAP-prescribed minimum preservation window we should state for enterprise customers?
- Marissa: can Legal sign off on the wording for auditor statements (we should avoid implying we keep user content)?
- Sophie: if you can share the auditor's exact ask, we’ll prepare a formal evidence statement we can attach to your compliance folder.

Happy to schedule a 30-min sync if that would speed this along.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Neha / Marissa — looping you in to draft a customer-facing statement for Acme. Below is the proposed wording we can provide to auditors. Please review and flag anything we should tighten.

Proposed evidence-statement (draft):
"Redwood Inference retains accounting artifacts necessary to comply with applicable accounting and tax obligations. For customers on Redwood's hosted and Dedicated offerings:

- Invoice artifacts (invoice number, date, amount, tax breakdown, payment status, and invoice PDF) are retained for a minimum of seven (7) years from the invoice date to satisfy accounting, tax, and audit requirements.
- Detailed request/response payloads and user-generated content are subject to deletion upon a valid Data Subject Request (DSR). For hosted customers the default operational retention window for detailed usage logs is ninety (90) days, unless a different retention schedule has been contractually agreed.
- To support customer reconciliation and audit requests, Redwood can provide an \"invoice evidence bundle\" containing invoice headers, aggregates, timestamps, and one-way hashed account identifiers (salting + hashing), which does not expose user-identifiable fields.

This statement is intended to describe Redwood's standard retention and evidence options; it does not create any legal rights beyond the parties' governing agreements."

We can implement the evidence bundle as a zipped export with the following spec: invoice PDF(s), invoice-index.csv (invoice_id, period_start, period_end, amount, currency, payment_status, hashed_account_id), and a summary.json with retention provenance. I attached a proposed spec (proposed-evidence-bundle-spec.json).

Neha: can Finance confirm 7 years is the conservative baseline we want on the record? Marissa: can Legal suggest language adjustments (esp. the last paragraph and the EU residency sentence)?

If all good, I will send this verbatim to Acme and generate a redacted 12-month export.

Thanks —
Kimberly

Hi Sophie — apologies for the delay. We reviewed with Finance and Legal and can confirm the following statement for your auditors. Please see the attached finalized PDF (acme-invoice-evidence-statement.pdf) and the DocuSign link for a countersigned copy if required.

Finalized (customer-facing) statement:
- Redwood retains invoice artifacts (invoice number, invoice PDF, billed amounts, tax breakdowns, and payment status) for a minimum of seven years to meet accounting and tax obligations.
- Detailed usage payloads (raw prompts/response content) are eligible for removal under a DSR and are not preserved as part of the invoice evidence bundle.
- For reconciliation, Redwood will provide an invoice evidence bundle that contains invoice PDFs and a CSV index including a one-way hashed account identifier (salted hash) rather than PII. The hash allows matching to your internal ledger without revealing user identifiers.
- For EU-hosted customers, invoice artifacts and the evidence bundle can be provided from EU-only storage (we will mark exports as EU-resident on request).

Next steps:
1) We will generate a redacted 12-month export and upload it to the shared drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_acme/InvoiceEvidence
2) If your auditors require a countersigned statement, please use the DocuSign link we provided: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ACME-Invoice-Evidence-Statement
3) If you want the hashed identifier to use a custom salt (so it matches your internal hash), send the salt in a secure channel and we can re-run the export.

Please let us know if this satisfies the audit. If not, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk through exported samples.
